title: Municipal Agencies
overview: Municipal agencies is a short syllabus unit (2 of the 77 course hours), but agency-matching questions are easy points, and the same boards reappear in land use, tax and property management questions. This chapter covers how New York's counties, cities, towns and villages divide power; what the legislative body, planning board, zoning board of appeals, architectural review board, conservation advisory council, landmark commission, building department, assessor, receiver of taxes, engineer and county health department each do; county referral under GML §239-m; SEQR roles; and the Open Meetings Law and FOIL. It then covers New York City's agencies, the ULURP clock and the 2025 Charter amendments that created faster housing approvals. **Classic exam content** is the agency-to-function matching plus the planning board, ZBA and Article 78 rules; county referral, SEQR, the open-government laws and NYC's agencies and ULURP add depth. The 2025 NYC Charter changes and the 2026 SEQR housing exemptions are **recent updates the exam may not test yet**, and they're labeled as recent wherever they appear. The big theme: elected legislative bodies make the rules, appointed boards apply them, and advisory bodies only advise.

mustKnow: The elected **legislative body** (city council, town board, village board of trustees) adopts local laws, zoning, **rezonings**, the comprehensive plan, the budget and the tax levy.
The **planning board** (appointed, 5 or 7 members) reviews **subdivision plats** and **site plans** and advises; it doesn't adopt the plan or grant variances.
The **ZBA** (appointed, 3 or 5 members) is **quasi-judicial**: appeals, interpretations, **use and area variances**, and some special permits. It can't rezone.
Town board members can't serve on the town ZBA or planning board; village trustees can't serve on the village ZBA or planning board.
Town zoning covers only land **outside incorporated villages**; villages zone their own land; New York counties generally don't zone.
The town **supervisor** presides over the town board and votes; a village board is the **mayor plus four trustees** by default.
Zoning must be **in accordance with the comprehensive plan**, which the legislative body adopts.
**Cluster development**: the planning board, if authorized by the town board, groups homes to save open space without raising density.
**Use variance**: **unnecessary hardship**, meaning no reasonable return from any permitted use (financial proof), a unique hardship, no change in neighborhood character, and not self-created.
**Area variance**: the owner's benefit is weighed against detriment to the neighborhood using five factors; self-created difficulty doesn't automatically bar it.
A **special use permit** is for a use the zoning already lists for the district; meet its standards, no hardship needed.

Votes count **all members**, not those present: ZBA and planning board majorities, the §239-m **majority plus one**, and the protest-petition **three-fourths**. The one exception: a ZBA rehearing needs a unanimous vote of the members present.
Building inspector's zoning ruling → **ZBA** appeal within 60 days → **Article 78** within **30 days** after the ZBA decision is filed.
Article 78 asks only whether the decision was illegal, **arbitrary and capricious** or irrational; the court doesn't rehear the case.
**ARB** approval covers appearance only; a building permit is still required.
The **CAC** inventories open space and wetlands and advises; it can become a **conservation board**. Neither issues DEC permits.
**Building department**: permits, inspections, **certificates of occupancy**, violations. A permit authorizes work; the CO confirms it.
The **assessor** values; the **legislative body** sets the levy and rate; the **receiver of taxes** collects; the **board of assessment review** hears grievances.
The **county health department** approves septic systems, wells, and water and sewer plans for **realty subdivisions** (5 or more lots of 5 acres or less within 3 years).
**GML §239-m**: plans, zoning changes, special permits, site plans and variances within **500 feet** of listed features go to the county before final action.
County disapproval or modification → the board needs a **majority plus one of all members** and must report its reasons to the county within 30 days.
A SEQR **lead agency** must be an **involved agency**; an **interested agency** only comments; the DEC Commissioner settles lead-agency disputes after 30 days.

SEQR: **Type I** (likely significant; Full EAF), **Type II** (no review, such as ministerial building permits), **Unlisted** (the rest). **Negative declaration** = no EIS; **positive declaration** = EIS; a **conditioned negative declaration** is for Unlisted actions only.
**Open Meetings Law**: 72-hour notice for meetings set a week ahead; **executive session** only for listed subjects, by a majority of the total membership; **ZBA** deliberations must be public.
**FOIL** covers records: 5 business days to respond; 30 days to appeal a denial.

NYC: **DOB** permits and COs; **BSA** variances and DOB appeals; **DCP/CPC** zoning changes and ULURP; **LPC** landmarks; **HPD** housing code and registration; **DEP** water and sewer; **DOF** assessments, taxes, ACRIS; **OATH** summonses.
**ULURP**: certification → community board 60 → borough president 30 → CPC 60 → Council 50 → mayor 5 → override 10. Community board and borough president votes are **advisory**.

Zoning **map** changes go through ULURP; zoning **text** amendments and **BSA variances** don't (text changes still get CPC and Council review). Since 2025, modest qualifying map changes can use ELURP instead.

**Recent update (2025 NYC Charter; may not be tested yet)**: ELURP and the Affordable Housing Fast Track end at the CPC in about 90 days; the BSA can fast-track publicly financed affordable housing; the **Affordable Housing Appeals Board** (2 of 3 votes) can reverse Council denials or modifications of qualifying affordable-housing applications; even-year elections failed. Standard ULURP still ends with the Council.

traps.trap: The ZBA can rezone an area if enough owners want it.
traps.truth: Rezoning is a legislative act of the town board, city council or village board. The ZBA gives relief to single parcels and interprets the law.

traps.trap: The planning board adopts the comprehensive plan and zoning.
traps.truth: The legislative body adopts both; the planning board prepares, reviews and recommends.

traps.trap: A majority of the members present is enough.
traps.truth: ZBA and planning board actions need a majority of all members; a §239-m override needs a majority plus one of all members; a protest petition needs three-fourths of all board members.

traps.trap: If the county ignores a §239-m referral, the project is disapproved.
traps.truth: After 30 days of silence the board may act without the report. Only a disapproval or modification recommendation (even a late one received at least 2 days before final action) triggers majority plus one.

traps.trap: A ZBA is quasi-judicial, so it may deliberate in private.
traps.truth: The Open Meetings Law exempts quasi-judicial proceedings except those of zoning boards of appeals. A ZBA deliberates and votes in public.

traps.trap: 72 hours is the FOIL response time.
traps.truth: 72 hours is the Open Meetings Law notice period; FOIL requires a response within 5 business days.

traps.trap: A neighbor has 4 months to sue over a town ZBA variance.
traps.truth: Town Law allows 30 days after the decision is filed with the town clerk; 4 months is the general Article 78 limit.

traps.trap: The town board can overrule its ZBA.
traps.truth: ZBA decisions go to State Supreme Court by Article 78. The town board, Department of State and county clerk can't reverse them.

traps.trap: An issued building permit means the work is approved.
traps.truth: A permit only authorizes work. A final inspection and a CO or certificate of compliance show completion; an old open permit isn't grandfathered.

traps.trap: If the assessor's record card lists an apartment, it's legal.
traps.truth: The assessor records features for taxes. Legality depends on zoning and the building department's permits and CO.

traps.trap: A conservation advisory council member can confirm a wet area isn't a regulated wetland.
traps.truth: The CAC only advises. Get a written jurisdictional determination from DEC and check federal and local rules.

traps.trap: A community board or borough president 'no' kills a ULURP application.
traps.truth: Their recommendations are advisory; the City Planning Commission and City Council decide.

traps.trap: Every NYC zoning, variance and landmark matter goes through ULURP.
traps.truth: BSA variances, LPC actions and zoning text amendments have their own procedures. ULURP covers zoning map changes, CPC special permits, city property deals and similar actions.

traps.trap: ULURP takes 240 days because each step gets 60.
traps.truth: 60 + 30 + 60 + 50 = 200 days; a veto and override can add 15 more.

traps.trap: Any old building is a landmark, and State Register listing blocks changes.
traps.truth: Only designation by the LPC or a local landmark commission restricts alterations, and an NYC landmark must be at least 30 years old. State or National Register listing doesn't restrict a private owner's work unless state or federal funding, licenses or permits are involved.

traps.trap: Since the 2025 Charter changes, NYC rezonings no longer go to the City Council.
traps.truth: Only qualifying ELURP and Affordable Housing Fast Track applications end at the CPC. Standard ULURP rezonings still get a Council vote and a possible mayoral veto, and the new tracks are recent enough that the exam may not test them.

mnemonics.name: Make it, plan it, bend it
mnemonics.meaning: The legislative body makes the rules (zoning, rezoning, budget, tax rate); the planning board plans and reviews layouts (master plan, plats, site plans); the ZBA bends the rules for one parcel (variances, interpretations).

mnemonics.name: ULURP 60-30-60-50
mnemonics.meaning: Community board 60, borough president 30, City Planning Commission 60, City Council 50 = 200 days; then mayor 5 and override 10.

mnemonics.name: Lead must be involved
mnemonics.meaning: A SEQR lead agency must have power to fund, approve or undertake the action; an interested agency, such as a CAC, can only comment.

formulas.name: Majority plus one (GML §239-m)
formulas.formula: Majority = (all members ÷ 2, rounded down) + 1; override = majority + 1

formulas.name: Protest-petition vote (Town Law §265)
formulas.formula: Votes needed = all board members × 3/4, rounded up

formulas.name: Unused floor area (FAR)
formulas.formula: Maximum floor area = lot area × FAR; unused = maximum − existing

sections.heading: How local government is organized in New York
sections.intro: Every parcel is in a county and in either a city or a town; some town land is also inside a village. The layer decides who zones and taxes it.
points: **Counties** run regional services: the county clerk records deeds and plats, the county health department approves septic and water systems, and the county planning agency reviews §239-m referrals. Counties generally don't zone.
**Cities** run under their own charters, with an elected council and a mayor (a strong mayor with a veto, a weak mayor, or a council-appointed city manager).
**Towns** cover all land outside cities (and Indian reservations), but town zoning applies only **outside incorporated villages** (Town Law §261).
**Villages** sit inside towns. Village residents pay town taxes too, but the village board of trustees zones village land, so check for a village before reading any zoning map.
**Home rule** lets local governments pass local laws consistent with state law. School and special districts (fire, water, sewer) tax but never zone.
**New York City** is one city of five boroughs, each also a county, with no towns or villages. It uses its Charter, Zoning Resolution and own agencies instead of the Town and Village Law.

sections.heading: The legislative body: council, town board, village board
sections.intro: If a question asks who changes the law, the zoning map, the budget or the tax rate, the answer is the elected legislative body.
points: Powers: local laws, the **zoning ordinance and map** and their amendments (**rezoning**), the **comprehensive plan** and **official map**, the **budget and tax levy** (which produces the rate), cluster authorization, **moratoria**, and **eminent domain** decisions.
It creates and fills the appointed boards (planning board, ZBA, CAC, ARB, landmark commission). In a village, the mayor appoints planning board and ZBA members with trustee approval.
The **town board** is the elected supervisor, who presides and votes, plus council members. The **village board of trustees** is the mayor plus four trustees by default.

Town rezoning steps: a hearing after at least **10 days'** published notice; written notice at least 10 days ahead to the clerk of any city, village, town or county whose boundary is within 500 feet (and to the state park commission or housing authority for a state park, parkway or public housing project within 500 feet); §239-m county referral; and SEQR review.

**Protest petition** (Town Law §265): if owners of **20%** of the land in the change, or of the land within **100 feet** adjacent or directly opposite, file a written protest, passage needs **three-fourths of all board members**. Villages match this (two-thirds on a three-member board).
The legislative body is not an appeals court for the ZBA; ZBA decisions are challenged in court.

example.title: Worked example: a protest-petition vote
steps: Owners of 25% of the land within 100 feet of a proposed rezoning file a written protest with a 5-member town board.
25% is at least 20%, so three-fourths applies: 5 × 3/4 = 3.75.
Round up, since there are no partial votes: 4 yes votes.
A 7-member board would need 7 × 3/4 = 5.25, rounded up to 6.
Answer: 4 of 5 (6 of 7). Without a protest, 3 of 5 would pass it.

sections.heading: The planning board and planning staff
sections.intro: The planning board is the appointed land-use reviewer and adviser. It reviews how land is divided and laid out; it doesn't legislate or grant variances.
points: A town board may create one by local law with **5 or 7** members, whom it appoints; staggered terms last as many years as the board has members. Town board members are ineligible, and alternates can fill in for conflicts.
Members need **4 hours of training a year** unless waived. Skipping it can cost reappointment, but no board decision is voided.

**Subdivision**: it reviews preliminary and final plats and may require improvements or a performance bond, plus parkland or a fee in lieu. The signed final plat must be filed with the county clerk within **62 days** or approval expires.
**Site plan review** covers parking, access, lighting, drainage and landscaping for a **permitted** use. If the use isn't permitted, the applicant first needs a use variance or rezoning.
It prepares or reviews the **comprehensive (master) plan** and advises other boards; the legislative body adopts the plan.
**Cluster development** (Town Law §278): with town board authorization, it may allow smaller lots that group homes and preserve open space, with no more units than a conventional layout.
A **planning department** is professional staff that advises but doesn't vote. In NYC, the Department of City Planning serves the City Planning Commission.

sections.heading: The zoning board of appeals and Article 78
sections.intro: The ZBA is zoning's safety valve: an appointed, administrative and quasi-judicial body that applies legal standards to one property at a time. It interprets the ordinance but doesn't make policy.
points: **Membership**: 3 or 5 members appointed by the legislative body (in a village, by the mayor with trustee approval), staggered terms equal to the board size, and 4 hours of training a year. Legislative-body members are ineligible.

**Appellate jurisdiction**: it hears appeals from the zoning officer's or building inspector's orders, interpretations and determinations, filed within **60 days**. An appeal usually stays enforcement.

**Procedure**: a hearing on at least **5 days'** published notice (with mailed notice to the parties and, when §239-m applies, the county); a decision within **62 days** after the hearing; filing with the clerk within **5 business days**.
**Votes**: a majority of **all members**, regardless of absences; an appeal that falls short is denied by default. A rehearing needs a unanimous vote of the members present.
It must grant the **minimum variance** needed, and any conditions must relate to the land and its use, because a variance runs with the land. It can't waive private deed covenants.

**Article 78** (CPLR) is the court challenge in State Supreme Court, due within **30 days** after a ZBA or planning board decision is filed with the town clerk (the general limit is 4 months). The court asks whether the decision was illegal, arbitrary and capricious or irrational; it doesn't rehear the case. The town board can't reverse a ZBA.

example.title: Worked example: a ZBA deadline chain
steps: The building inspector's permit denial is filed March 2, so the owner's ZBA appeal is due within 60 days: by May 1.
The ZBA holds its hearing May 20 and must decide within 62 days: by July 21.
It grants a variance July 15 and files the decision with the town clerk July 17.
A neighbor's Article 78 petition is due 30 days after filing: by August 16.
Answer: 60 days to appeal, 62 days to decide, 30 days to sue.

sections.heading: Who does what: the other local offices
sections.intro: Exam questions often describe a problem and ask which office handles it. Match the function, then confirm locally, because titles and delegated powers vary.
points: Approvals don't substitute for each other. Converting a barn into a restaurant can need zoning (use, site plan or special permit), building (code, CO), health (septic, food service) and engineering (access, drainage) sign-offs.
Rely on written answers from the office with authority, not a board member's remark, a seller's story or a neighbor's experience.
Permitted uses come from the current zoning text and map; the assessor's property class code is a tax label that grants no development rights.

sections.heading: Building permits, certificates of occupancy and code enforcement
sections.intro: Outside NYC, the NYS Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code applies everywhere and is usually enforced by the city, town or village (see the opt-out chain below). NYC has its own Construction Codes, enforced by its Department of Buildings.
points: A **building permit** authorizes work; inspections follow; a **certificate of occupancy** (new buildings, changes of use) or **certificate of compliance** (other work) confirms compliance. A temporary CO can allow occupancy of finished, safe portions.
An **open permit** (issued but never finaled) is a red flag; age doesn't grandfather it, and the seller usually must close it out.

**Opt-out chain** (Executive Law §381): if a city, town or village opts out of enforcing the Uniform Code, the **county** enforces it; if the county opts out too, the **Department of State** does. The code always applies.
Stricter local construction standards need State Code Council approval, and Uniform Code variances come from Department of State regional boards of review, not the ZBA.
A building permit for a conforming house is **ministerial** (no discretion), so it's Type II under SEQR and isn't referred to the county.
A unit is legal only if zoning allows it and the building file supports it; tax records, rental history and listing descriptions don't legalize it.

sections.heading: Health, water and environmental approvals
sections.intro: Rural and suburban deals often turn on wells, septic systems and wetlands. Those approvals come from health and environmental agencies, not zoning boards.
points: The **county health department** (or a State Health Department office where the county has none) approves septic designs and private water supplies; local sanitary codes may be stricter than state minimums.

**Realty subdivision** (Public Health Law §1115): a tract divided into **5 or more residential lots of 5 acres or less** within any 3 years needs health department approval of water and sewage plans before lots are sold, leased or offered.
Reliable well-water results come from a lab certified under the State Health Department's **ELAP** program, not a home kit or the seller's disclosure.

**Wetlands**: DEC regulates freshwater wetlands of **12.4 acres** or more (**7.4 acres** from January 1, 2028) and wetlands DEC mapped before January 1, 2025 (including mapped wetlands of unusual local importance), plus a **100-foot adjacent area**; the Adirondack Park Agency covers the Adirondack Park. DEC narrowed its reach after an April 8, 2026 Albany County Supreme Court decision on its wetland rules, so get DEC's written **jurisdictional determination** and check Army Corps and local rules.
A CAC or local wetlands commission studies and advises (or runs a local permit law); it can't replace DEC.

sections.heading: County planning referral: GML §239-m, §239-n and §239-nn
sections.intro: Some local decisions affect people beyond town lines, so state law routes them past the county planning agency before final action.
points: **What** (§239-m): adopting or amending a comprehensive plan or zoning law, special use permits, site plans, use or area variances, and other zoning authorizations. Subdivision plats go under **§239-n**.

**Where**: land within **500 feet** of a city, town or village boundary; a county or state park; a county or state road, parkway or expressway; a county drainage channel; county or state land with a public building; or a farm in an agricultural district (not for area variances). Schools, churches and private golf courses don't count.
Not referred: ministerial acts such as a building permit for a conforming house, or actions the county agrees in writing are of local concern only.

The county has **30 days** after receiving a **full statement** (application plus environmental assessment form) to recommend approval, modification or disapproval. If it misses that, the board may act, but a late report received at least **2 days** before final action still counts.

After a **disapproval or modification** recommendation, the board can act contrary only by a **majority plus one of all its members**, and must report its final action and reasons to the county within **30 days**. Skipping a required referral can void the approval.

**§239-nn**: a hearing on a special use permit, use variance, site plan or subdivision within 500 feet of an adjacent municipality requires notice to that municipality's clerk at least **10 days** before. The neighbor may be heard but its consent isn't needed (NYC is excluded).

example.title: Worked example: overriding the county
steps: A 5-member ZBA refers a use variance for land 300 feet from a county road, and the county recommends disapproval within 30 days.
Majority of all 5 = 3, so majority plus one = 4.
Only 4 members attend and vote 3–1 to grant. It fails, because the count uses all members, not those present.
Answer: 4 yes votes, plus a report of reasons to the county within 30 days.

sections.heading: SEQR: who reviews environmental impacts
sections.intro: The State Environmental Quality Review Act (ECL Article 8; 6 NYCRR Part 617) makes state and local agencies weigh environmental impacts before approving, funding or carrying out a discretionary action.
points: **Type I** actions are listed as likely to be significant (for example, adopting a comprehensive plan or first zoning law, or changing allowed uses on 25 or more acres) and need a Full EAF and, when several agencies are involved, coordinated review. **Type II** actions need no review (ministerial building permits, area variances for 1–3 family homes, a 1–3 family home on an approved lot). Everything else is **Unlisted**.

A **negative declaration** means no significant adverse impact and no EIS; a **positive declaration** requires an EIS; a **conditioned negative declaration** is only for Unlisted actions, with mitigation conditions and a comment period of at least 30 days.

EIS path: required **scoping** → draft EIS → public comment (at least 30 days, and at least 10 days after any hearing) → final EIS → written **findings** by each involved agency → decision. No involved agency may approve before SEQR is complete.
Typical involved agencies: the town board for a rezoning, the planning board for a site plan or subdivision, the ZBA for a use variance, DEC for a state permit. A CAC is usually an interested agency.

**Recent update (May 2026; the exam may not test it yet)**: the FY2027 state budget, signed May 27, 2026, exempts many housing projects on previously disturbed land connected to existing water and sewer from SEQR (including NYC's CEQR), up to unit caps (NYC: 250 citywide, 500 in medium- and high-density areas; 300 in other urbanized areas; 100 in non-urbanized areas; 20 where there's no zoning), and sets a 2-year deadline to finish an EIS. Zoning, permits and other environmental rules still apply.
NYC applies SEQR through **CEQR**, with a city agency such as DCP as lead agency for land-use applications.

sections.heading: Open Meetings Law and FOIL
sections.intro: Two separate laws open local government: the Open Meetings Law, or Sunshine Law (Public Officers Law Article 7), covers meetings; the Freedom of Information Law (Article 6) covers records.
points: **Executive session** subjects are limited to public safety, law-enforcement matters, litigation, collective bargaining, a particular person's medical, financial or employment history (or hiring, discipline or firing), exams, and the **proposed acquisition, sale or lease of real property** (or securities) when publicity would substantially affect its value. No formal vote to spend public money may be taken there.

Exempt from the Open Meetings Law: judicial and quasi-judicial proceedings **except zoning boards of appeals** (and the Public Service Commission), political caucuses, and matters made confidential by law.

**Minutes** are due within **2 weeks**; minutes of a vote taken in executive session within **1 week**. A public hearing (comments) differs from a meeting (deliberation), and an open meeting doesn't guarantee a right to speak.
FOIL lets a licensee request a town's permit file, violation history or ZBA decisions, but privacy, security and internal pre-decision memos may be withheld.

sections.heading: New York City agencies
sections.intro: NYC has no town boards or village ZBAs. Its land-use and building functions are split among agencies created by the City Charter.
points: **HPD registration**: every multiple dwelling (3 or more units) and every 1–2 family home where neither the owner nor an immediate family member lives must register yearly; an unregistered owner can't bring a nonpayment case. HPD doesn't issue COs.

**HPD violation classes**: A non-hazardous (90 days to correct), B hazardous (30 days), C immediately hazardous (generally 24 hours, with a few exceptions such as 21 days for lead paint; no heat in heat season is Class C). There is no Class D.

**LPC permits**: staff issue a Certificate of No Effect for DOB-permitted work that doesn't affect protected features and a Permit for Minor Work for rule-compliant work that does; work outside LPC's rules, such as a visible rooftop addition, demolition or new construction, needs a **Certificate of Appropriateness** from the full Commission after a public hearing.

**Landmarks** may be individual, interior, scenic or historic districts and must be at least **30 years** old. Interior landmarks must be customarily open or accessible to the public, so a private apartment doesn't qualify.

**BSA variance findings** (ZR §72-21): unique physical conditions, no reasonable return (not required for nonprofits), no harm to neighborhood character, hardship **not created by the owner or a predecessor**, and the **minimum variance**.

**Taxes**: DOF mails the Notice of Property Value each January; the separate **NYC Tax Commission** hears assessment appeals; the **City Council** fixes tax rates. ACRIS covers Manhattan, the Bronx, Brooklyn and Queens; Staten Island records go to the Richmond County Clerk.

sections.heading: NYC zoning and building records to check
sections.intro: Most NYC deal problems show up in DOB, HPD, DEP and DOF records. Know what each document proves.
points: The **certificate of occupancy** fixes legal use and unit count; an extra unit is illegal until DOB amends the CO. Buildings finished **before 1938** generally need no CO unless use, egress or occupancy changed; DOB can issue a **Letter of No Objection** confirming use.

**Multiple Dwelling Law §§301–302**: an owner can't collect rent or sue for nonpayment for periods a multiple dwelling is occupied without the required residential CO (compliant Loft Law units excepted).
**Districts**: R (residence), C (commercial), M (manufacturing). **C1 and C2 overlays** on residential blocks allow local retail; overlays are zoning, not landmark, designations.

**Nonconforming use**: stop substantially all of it for **2 continuous years** and only conforming uses may follow, whatever the owner intended (ZR §52-61). City of Yes for Economic Opportunity (2024) lets some vacant ground-floor storefronts in residential districts reopen for local retail or offices, but it doesn't revive uses like auto repair.

**FISP (Local Law 11)**: buildings over **6 stories** need facade inspections every **5 years**. **Local Law 97** caps carbon emissions for most buildings over **25,000 square feet**. Both can mean big co-op or condo costs.

Paying an OATH penalty doesn't clear a DOB violation; the owner must certify correction. Unpaid **DEP water and sewer charges** are liens, so they're paid or escrowed at closing. **FAR** = floor area ÷ lot area; unused floor area is marketed as **air rights**.

example.title: Worked example: unused floor area (air rights)
steps: Lot: 25 × 100 = 2,500 square feet; district maximum FAR 3.0.
Maximum floor area = 2,500 × 3.0 = 7,500 square feet.
Unused = 7,500 − 5,500 existing = 2,000 square feet.
Answer: 2,000 square feet. Traps: 7,500 ignores the building; 2,500 is the lot area.

sections.heading: ULURP step by step
sections.intro: The Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (NYC Charter §§197-c and 197-d) is the city's fixed-clock public review for major land-use actions: advisory reviews first, binding votes last.
points: ULURP covers zoning **map** changes, CPC special permits, City Map changes, city facility sites, city property acquisitions and dispositions, housing and urban renewal plans, franchises and revocable consents, landfills and subdivision mapping.

Not ULURP: zoning **text** amendments (CPC hearing and vote with community and borough comment, then Council review), **BSA** variances and special permits, and LPC designations and permits. Since 2025, some qualifying actions use ELURP instead (next section).
Community board and borough president recommendations are **advisory**; if either fails to act or waives review, the application moves on.
If the CPC misses its deadline, the application is generally deemed denied; if the Council misses its 50 days, the CPC decision stands.

example.title: Worked example: the ULURP clock
steps: Community board 60 + borough president 30 = 90 days of advisory review.
CPC 60 brings the total to 150; City Council 50 brings it to 200.
Mayoral veto 5 + override 10 = 215 days at most.
Answer: the four sequential review periods total 200 days, about seven months.

sections.heading: The 2025 NYC Charter changes and recent updates
sections.intro: On November 4, 2025, NYC voters approved four Charter Revision Commission proposals (Questions 2–5): three reshape land-use review for housing (two fast tracks, ELURP and an appeals board), and one creates a digital City Map. A fifth, Question 6, moving city elections to even years, failed. **All of this is recent**: the state exam is built on the DOS syllabus and may not test it yet, so answer an ordinary ULURP question with the classic steps.
points: Unchanged: ULURP still governs most rezonings, community boards keep a 60-day review in every track, and the Charter changes don't alter environmental review or landmark protections (the separate 2026 state SEQR exemptions can remove environmental review for some housing).

**Exam angle**: the classic answer, in the syllabus and older books, is that an NYC rezoning ends with a Council vote and a possible mayoral veto, and that's still true for standard ULURP. The exceptions are new: qualifying ELURP and Fast Track applications end at the CPC, BSA fast-track approvals skip ULURP, and Council denials or modifications of qualifying affordable housing can be reversed by the Affordable Housing Appeals Board.

Earlier Charter changes still in force: **2018** community board term limits (4 consecutive 2-year terms); **2019** a project summary 30 days before ULURP certification and longer community board review for June (90 days) and July 1–15 (75 days) certifications.

example.title: Worked example: ULURP vs ELURP timeline
steps: ELURP: 60 (community board and borough president together) + 30 (CPC) = 90 days.
Savings: 200 − 90 = 110 days, about 3.6 months, with no Council vote.
A Fast Track rezoning that needs an EIS: 60 + 45 = 105 days.
Answer: about 90 days, with the CPC as final decision-maker.
